primary_source_review.title: Integrable Systems and Isomonodromy Deformations
locations: Section 9 page 43: arbitrary finite constant lower-flow combinations
Theorem 9.1 and Lemma 9.3, pages 44-46: forward sectorial solutions, fixed phase and constant Stokes matrices
Section 8 pages 36-39: companion shearing and first-row injectivity argument
application: Monic depressed scalar differential operator of arbitrary order n; highest flow m coprime to n.
All lower flows have constant coefficients, as required by the page-43 remark.
Leading matrix J^m has distinct fixed eigenvalues.
Finite spectral companion equation is polynomial and ordinary at zero.
Analytic continuation compares actual existing algebraic branches with BOTH the same full formal phase and the same right Stokes matrices.
The proof uses the correctly oriented left ratio and rederives its first-row consequence for every n.
primary_source_review.not_used: No generic inverse-data solvability or arbitrary resonant reconstruction from Theorem 9.5.
primary_source_review.review: Actual retained primary PDF inspected by root and jacobian_dixmier_audit; internal review.

written_new_arguments: Finite exact residue primitive of one for every scalar commutator using res[P,Q P^(-1/n)].
All-coprime-order scalar algebraic branching exclusion by the precisely scoped forward-Stokes input.
Single weighted infinity bracket, with lower flows and derivative corrections strictly lower.
All-prime-order finite mate normal form over the original constant field.
Constant-uniformizer valued specialization obstruction allowing a nonunit leading coefficient.
scope: Finite scalar differential operators over one-variable characteristic-zero algebraic function fields. Long application retains the exact-first-image scalar chart and regular classical orders 2 and 3. Composite common-divisor orders, changed first images and matrix carriers remain open.

additional_primary_review.exact_location: Section 53.12, characteristic-zero tame ramification formula; Lemma 53.12.2
additional_primary_review.application: The compactified coefficient curve has no finite ramification; all residue fields are algebraically closed constants, so total infinity ramification is d-b.
